title: Tenant cert rotation caused operator state mismatch — design roll-forward remediation and hotfix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several on-prem customers reported failed upgrades and partial service outages after automated tenant certificate rotation completed. Operator reconcile loops encountered a state mismatch where CRs appeared present in Kubernetes but the operator's in-memory projection (KV cache) and helm post-upgrade verification diverged, preventing normal rollforward of the upgrade. This ticket tracks root cause, immediate mitigations, and an engineered hotfix that prefers roll-forward reconciliation rather than aggressive rollback in the presence of cert/secret churn.
observed_customer_reports: Customer A: control-plane reported 'Upgrade hung waiting for webhook' and app-level errors after nightly cert rotation
Customer B: tenant processes restarted repeatedly until manual intervention; ops reported helm Release in 'pending-upgrade' state
Customer C: partial feature regressions post-upgrade; console showed operator reconcile errors referencing secret UID mismatch
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure an on-prem cluster with Redwood operator v2.14.0 and nodeagent
2) Schedule an automated rotation of tenant TLS certs via external KMS/Secret controller
3) Trigger operator-managed helm upgrade (minor runtime patch) concurrently with cert rotation window
4) Observe operator reconcile logs: repeated failures to verify helm post-upgrade hook, KV cache miss for rotated secret, and helm release state stuck in pending-upgrade
5) Reproduce by injecting a secret replace with new UID quickly after operator reads old secret to simulate race
root_cause_analysis: Primary root cause: operator relies on stable secret identities (UIDs) during upgrade verification; cert rotation replaced Secrets in-place resulting in UID/metadata churn that the operator treated as divergent state rather than updated credentials
Secondary contributor: helm post-upgrade hooks assume synchronous availability of supporting resources (nodeagent webhooks, mutating webhooks) which momentarily failed during secret rollout

Tertiary factor: operator's KV cache and reconcile idempotency gaps allowed a window where CRs were present in etcd but not reconciled into runtime projection, causing helm safety checks to fail and trigger rollback paths that did not complete cleanly
Telemetry gap: insufficient logging around secret rotation events and reconcile decision rationale made post-upgrade troubleshooting slow
temporary_mitigation: 1) For impacted customers, provide a runbook: pause automated cert rotation, manually reapply secrets with preserved UID (where possible) or perform a controlled upgrade outside rotation window
2) Run controller 'reconcile-resync' job to force operator to rebuild KV projection for affected tenants
3) Provide a customer-side helm command snippet to mark release as deployed (only when verified safe) to unblock workloads
4) Establish a concierge support escalation path for customers in production with immediate paging and cross-team SRE assistance
proposed_fix: A. Make operator reconcile idempotent across secret UID changes: treat Secret content equivalence (by certificate subject and fingerprint) as same logical credential rather than relying on Kubernetes UID

B. Add transient-rollforward logic: when helm post-upgrade verification fails due to transient webhook/secret flakiness, attempt controlled roll-forward reconciliation (reapply CRs, re-run health probes) before invoking rollback
C. Harden helm hooks and operator health-checks to tolerate short-lived webhook 5xx/503 during secret transition windows
D. Add a short-lived operator feature flag (enable_rollforward_on_secret_rotation) that gates rollout of the hotfix so we can canary safely
E. Emit structured telemetry when a reconcile decision is drawn from secret-change vs observed resource deletion to facilitate faster postmortems
rollout_strategy: Canary stage 1: operator-2.14.1-hotfix to 2 internal staging tenants; monitor 24h
Canary stage 2: 10% of onprem fleets (non-production first) across two cloud partners; monitor for failed upgrades and reconcile errors for 48h
Full rollout: if canaries stable, schedule progressive rollout with 1% increments and automated safety window for 24h checks between increments
Rollback policy: if increase in 'pending-upgrade' > baseline or any customer-facing outage within 2 hours of deployment, automatically pause rollout and notify oncall
Feature flag: ability to disable rollforward per-tenant in case customers prefer aggressive rollback semantics
testing_plan: Unit tests: secret equivalence comparator and reconcile decision logic (edge cases for certificate rotation and secret->TLS variations)
Integration tests: simulated cert rotation during helm upgrade in our CI harness using KinD clusters, cover both small and large manifests
Chaos tests: inject secret replacement races and webhook 503s during upgrade; assert operator completes rollforward path without leaving releases in pending state
Customer-like staging: coordinate with two pilot customers to run upgrade+rotation in their staging clusters before production rollout
Canary observability: pre-deploy synthetic upgrade jobs that validate health probes and helm release states post-upgrade
monitoring_and_alerting: Add metric: operator.reconcile.secret_equivalence_mismatch.count with tags tenant_id, cluster_region
Add metric: operator.upgrade.pending_release.count and a SLO-based alert if rate spikes > 3x baseline during rollout
Create dashboard: 'Onprem upgrade health' with per-tenant pending-upgrade, reconcile error rates, and secret-rotation events correlated
Alert runbook: PagerDuty oncall if any canary tenant reports pending-upgrade for >30 minutes after upgrade; quiet alerts for known transient conditions during canaries
Log enrichment: include pre/post secret fingerprint in reconcile logs and correlate with helm release events
docs_and_communication: Draft customer notification: explain cause (cert rotation race), interim mitigations, and planned hotfix timeline; coordinated with support and account teams
Internal runbook update: 'Onprem upgrade stuck during cert rotation' including safe manual commands and escalation matrix
Console messages: surface per-tenant advisory when automated cert rotation is scheduled overlapping with operator upgrade window
KB article: step-by-step guide for customers who prefer to disable automated cert rotation during scheduled operator upgrades
follow_up_tasks: Post-release audit: run discovery across all onprem tenants to detect historical secret UID flips that correlated with upgrades
Add e2e upgrade+rotation test to periodic nightly CI to prevent regression
Product discussion: decide whether tenant-facing control should be offered to lock cert rotation windows via Console
Schedule a postmortem with SRE, Support, Product, and Security within 72 hours of release
